title: HiMOSS: A Novel High-dimensional Multi-objective Optimization Method via Adaptive Gradient-Based Subspace Sampling for Analog Circuit Sizing
problem: Analog circuit sizing requires optimizing multiple competing objectives (power, speed, area) simultaneously under high-dimensional design spaces with complex constraints, making exhaustive search and simulation-based optimization computationally prohibitive.
motivation: Efficient multi-objective optimization for analog circuit sizing accelerates design iteration cycles and enables better exploration of performance-power-area trade-offs critical to hardware development.
method: HiMOSS uses Bayesian optimization—learning from past design attempts to predict promising regions—to balance multiple competing objectives. To manage high-dimensional design spaces, it performs adaptive subspace sampling by constructing a smaller search space from gradient information (which direction improves performance) and previous successful designs, with older successes mattering less as the search progresses. Instead of running expensive circuit simulations, it estimates gradients quickly using sparse regression.
key_novelty: The innovation is using gradient approximations and success history—with earlier attempts weighted less over time—to adaptively reduce the search to the most important dimensions.
contributions: Lightweight Bayesian optimization with approximate constrained expected hypervolume improvement achieving constant complexity
Adaptive subspace sampling using gradients and previous success steps to handle high-dimensional optimization
Sparse regression-based gradient approximation without additional simulations
Empirical validation showing improvements over Bayesian and evolutionary optimization baselines

metrics.other: hypervolume improvement, convergence efficiency, solution quality

primary_theme: High-dimensional multi-objective analog circuit sizing optimization
